page: Microsoft Azure E8bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provides 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores of a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include dedicated CPU core allocation with two threads per core, 48 MB of L3 cache, and instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI. System memory totals 64.0 GB, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance includes 322 GB of local SSD temporary storage and features no bundled GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations position the E8bds_v5 consistently within the mid-range performance tier. Compute testing records a Geekbench single-core score of 1575.0 and a multi-core score of 5876.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 11359.84. Memory subsystems deliver an uncached read bandwidth of 58.26 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 40.64 GB/sec, supporting 7.99 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark database score of 4011.82. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and 7B LLM inference fall into lower performance quartiles, reflecting throughput limitations inherent to an 8-vCPU execution envelope.

By coupling 64 GB of system RAM with dedicated local NVMe-class SSD storage, the E8bds_v5 provides balanced resource density for memory-bound tasks without requiring high vCPU overhead. Workloads best aligned with this configuration include relational databases, in-memory caches like Redis, ETL batch processing, and medium-scale enterprise application backends requiring moderate processing capacity and substantial memory allocation.
description: Microsoft Azure E8bds_v5 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 4 physical cores with multithreading, 48 MB of L3 cache, and AVX-512 support. Storage consists of a bundled 322 GB local SSD, while GPU hardware is omitted. Benchmark results demonstrate stable median performance across standard compute and memory benchmarks, highlighted by 7.99 million Redis SET operations per second and 58.26 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth. Although complex multi-threaded compression and medium-sized LLM inference show architectural boundaries, the 8:1 memory-to-core ratio and dedicated local storage make the instance suitable for in-memory caching, relational database hosting, and memory-intensive enterprise business logic.
